contradictions.finding: All three cards identify the archived donor as the origin repository; none identifies edithatogo/archive-govt-nz as current origin authority.
contradictions.required_action: Supersede canonical card metadata while retaining donor lineage.

contradictions.finding: The historical card declares superseded_operational_dataset and historical, but its body calls the repository the live operational home and contains future upload instructions.
contradictions.required_action: Preserve historical role and remove active-operation implications in a superseding card revision only if authorised.

contradictions.finding: The open historical repository viewer converts manifests/validation_report.json into a one-row validation split instead of exposing the 6,609 record corpus.
contradictions.required_action: Treat viewer row count as unrelated to corpus record count; configure data files explicitly in a future authorised revision.

contradictions.finding: Canonical and DOI dataset APIs list RIGHTS.md, while anonymous resolve returns 401 because both repositories are auto-gated. File presence is true even when anonymous byte readback is unavailable.
contradictions.required_action: Readback must derive has_rights_statement from the exact-revision inventory and separately record content access/verification.

contradictions.finding: The historical API lists 6,610 raw_xml directory entries, of which raw_xml/README.md is documentation; the controlled manifest contains 6,609 raw content files matching 6,609 records.
contradictions.required_action: Count payload extensions or manifest members, not directory prefix alone.

cross_identity_comparison.unknown_reason: Canonical and DOI snapshot payload metadata is inaccessible without authentication under auto-gating; no count/root/schema is inferred from filenames.

publication_gate.minimum_action: Publish only the reviewed canonical card/state candidate to edithatogo/corpus-legislation-nz, then bind and independently read back the exact returned revision through the gated-access contract.
